interviewBank.q: What is HTML and what is it not?
interviewBank.answer: HTML is a markup language that describes the structure and meaning of content. It is not a programming language: it has no loops, variables or logic; CSS handles presentation and JavaScript handles behaviour.

interviewBank.q: How does a browser turn an HTML file into a page?
interviewBank.answer: It parses the bytes into characters, tokens and nodes, builds the DOM, combines it with CSS rules into a render tree, lays out the boxes and paints them. Scripts can change the DOM before or after painting.

interviewBank.q: Walk me through what happens between typing a URL and seeing the page.
interviewBank.answer: The browser resolves the host with DNS, opens a connection and negotiates TLS, sends an HTTP request, receives the response, parses HTML into the DOM, fetches CSS and scripts, builds the render tree, lays out boxes and paints, then runs scripts that may change the DOM.

interviewBank.q: Is HTML a programming language? How do you answer that in an interview?
interviewBank.answer: HTML is a markup language: it describes structure and meaning, with no variables, control flow or computation. The honest answer names what it is, then points out that the platform as a whole — HTML, CSS and JavaScript — is programmable.

interviewBank.q: When would you choose a static page over a dynamic one?
interviewBank.answer: When the content changes rarely and is the same for every visitor: static files cache well, cost less to serve and are easy to audit. A dynamic page is worth it when the response depends on the user, the data or the request.

defenseBank.q: A beginner says HTML is a programming language. How do you correct that gently?
defenseBank.answer: I show that HTML has no control flow or variables, then show where CSS and JavaScript fit, so the correction teaches the model instead of only naming it.
steps: Ask them what a program must be able to do.
Show that HTML only describes structure.
Show one CSS rule and one JavaScript line for contrast.

defenseBank.q: Why teach the document tree before tags?
defenseBank.answer: Once the tree is clear, nesting, indentation and closing tags stop being arbitrary rules and become the shape of the document.
steps: Draw a small page as a tree.
Map each node to a tag.
Show what happens when a branch is not closed.

mcqBank.q: Which language is responsible for the structure of a web page?
mcqBank.why: HTML describes structure and meaning; CSS styles it and JavaScript adds behaviour.

mcqBank.q: What does the browser build from the HTML document?
mcqBank.why: The document object model is the tree the browser parses and renders.

interviewBank.q: Why does the HTML file need a charset declaration?
interviewBank.answer: Without it the browser guesses the encoding and can misread non-ASCII characters. `meta charset="UTF-8"` states the encoding before the text is decoded.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between viewing source and inspecting the DOM?
interviewBank.answer: View source shows the bytes the server sent. The inspector shows the live DOM after parsing and any script changes, which is why the two can differ.

interviewBank.q: Why is index.html the entry point?
interviewBank.answer: It is the conventional directory index: a server maps a request for a folder to index.html, and every hosting platform supports it without configuration.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between opening a file with file:// and serving it over HTTP?
interviewBank.answer: A file URL has no origin, so modules, fetch and some storage APIs are restricted. Over HTTP the page has an origin, relative requests work the way they will in production, and cookies and service workers are available.

interviewBank.q: Which files belong in a project root?
interviewBank.answer: The entry document, the project configuration and top-level folders such as css, js, images and assets. Build output and dependencies stay out of version control.

defenseBank.q: A learner cannot see their changes. What do you check first?
defenseBank.answer: I check whether they saved the file and whether the browser is loading that same file, because those two account for most "nothing happened" reports.
steps: Confirm the address bar path matches the file.

defenseBank.q: Why insist on a folder per project?
defenseBank.answer: Relative paths only stay correct when the structure is stable. A predictable layout prevents broken images and stylesheets as the project grows.

mcqBank.q: Which file name does a web server use as the default page?
mcqBank.why: index.html is the conventional directory index.

mcqBank.q: Which meta tag controls mobile layout width?
mcqBank.why: The viewport meta tag tells the browser how to scale the layout on small screens.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between an id and a class?
interviewBank.answer: An id is unique in the document and is used for fragment links and one-off targeting. A class is reusable across many elements and is the normal styling hook.

interviewBank.q: What are void elements?
interviewBank.answer: Elements that cannot have content, such as `img`, `br`, `input` and `meta`. They have no closing tag; a trailing slash is allowed but not required in HTML.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between an attribute and a property?
interviewBank.answer: The attribute is what the markup declares; the property is the live value on the DOM object. They start equal but diverge: typing in an input changes the property, not the attribute.

interviewBank.q: When should you use a data-* attribute instead of a class?
interviewBank.answer: When the value is data for behaviour or configuration rather than a styling hook. Classes describe presentation patterns; data attributes carry values that scripts read.

interviewBank.q: Name three global attributes you actually use and say why.
interviewBank.answer: id for unique targets and labels, class for reusable styling hooks, and lang for language changes inside a document. Others worth naming are hidden, title, tabindex and data-*.

defenseBank.q: Why not use id for styling?

interviewBank.q: Why should heading levels not be chosen by size?
interviewBank.answer: Size is a styling decision for CSS. The heading level describes the document outline, and skipping levels breaks navigation for screen-reader users and weakens SEO structure.

interviewBank.q: When is blockquote appropriate?
interviewBank.answer: For an extended quotation from another source. Short inline quotations use `q`. Neither should be used just to indent text.

interviewBank.q: When is the br element the right choice?

interviewBank.q: strong versus b, em versus i — what is the difference?

interviewBank.q: How do you mark up a code snippet that contains angle brackets?
interviewBank.answer: Use pre and code and escape the less-than sign as an entity and the ampersand as its entity. Otherwise the parser treats the snippet as markup.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between absolute and relative URLs?
interviewBank.answer: An absolute URL contains the scheme and host and works from anywhere. A relative URL is resolved against the current document’s location, which keeps a project portable.

interviewBank.q: Why is target="_blank" paired with rel="noopener"?
interviewBank.answer: The new page receives window.opener unless noopener is set, which allows reverse tabnabbing. noopener severs that reference; noreferrer also hides the referrer.

interviewBank.q: How does the browser resolve a relative URL?
interviewBank.answer: Against the document’s base URL: the directory of the current page unless a base element says otherwise. That is why the same href resolves differently on pages in different folders.

interviewBank.q: What is reverse tabnabbing and how do you prevent it?
interviewBank.answer: A page opened with target blank can reach window.opener and navigate the original tab. The noopener relationship removes that reference; noreferrer also hides the referrer.

interviewBank.q: How would you structure navigation for a ten-page site?
interviewBank.answer: One shared nav with a short, stable set of top-level links, current-page indication, a skip link before it, and consistent order on every page. Deeper pages get breadcrumbs rather than more top-level items.

interviewBank.q: Why is scope important on a th element?
interviewBank.answer: It tells assistive technology whether the header applies to its column or its row, so each data cell is announced with the right label.

interviewBank.q: Why should tables not be used for page layout?
interviewBank.answer: A layout table has no data relationship, so screen readers announce meaningless row and column context, and the structure cannot reflow on small screens.

interviewBank.q: How do you make a table accessible?
interviewBank.answer: Add a caption, use header cells with scope col or row, keep one header per column or row, avoid layout tables, and make sure merged cells still leave every row with the right number of columns.

interviewBank.q: When is a table the wrong element?
interviewBank.answer: For page layout, for lists of unrelated items, and for anything that needs to reflow as a single column on a phone. If there is no row-and-column relationship, it is not tabular data.

interviewBank.q: What pitfalls come with rowspan and colspan?
interviewBank.answer: They change the grid, so later rows must supply the remaining cells; screen readers rely on the resulting header relationships, and responsive CSS cannot simply stack cells without breaking the pairing.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between GET and POST?
interviewBank.answer: GET appends the data to the URL, which makes it visible, bookmarkable and length-limited. POST sends it in the request body, which suits state-changing submissions and larger payloads.

interviewBank.q: Why does every input need a name attribute?
interviewBank.answer: The name is the key submitted with the value. Without it the field is not included in the form data at all.

interviewBank.q: GET or POST for a login form, and why?
interviewBank.answer: POST. GET puts the credentials in the URL, which is stored in history, server logs and referrer headers, and it can be triggered by a link or prefetch.

interviewBank.q: Why must every input have a name?
interviewBank.answer: The name is the key in the submitted form data. Without it the control is omitted from the submission entirely, no matter what the user typed.

interviewBank.q: What actually happens when a form submits?
interviewBank.answer: The browser validates the controls, builds a form data set from the successful controls, encodes it according to the method and enctype, sends the request to the action URL and navigates to the response.

defenseBank.q: A learner complains that clicking the label does nothing.
defenseBank.answer: I check that for matches an id exactly; a typo silently breaks the association.

defenseBank.q: Why not rely on placeholder instead of label?
defenseBank.answer: A placeholder disappears as soon as typing starts and is not a reliable accessible name. The label stays visible and is announced.

mcqBank.q: Which method sends form data in the URL query string?
mcqBank.why: GET appends the fields to the URL.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute associates a label with an input?
mcqBank.why: The for value must equal the input id.

interviewBank.q: Is native HTML validation enough for security?
interviewBank.answer: No. It improves user experience but can be bypassed by disabling JavaScript, editing the DOM or sending a direct request. The server must validate every field again.

interviewBank.q: When should an input be disabled instead of readonly?
interviewBank.answer: Readonly keeps the value submitted but prevents editing. Disabled removes the control from submission and from the tab order, so it is for values that must not be sent.

interviewBank.q: Client-side validation versus server-side — what do you tell a junior?
interviewBank.answer: Client-side validation is a convenience for the user; server-side validation is the security boundary. The client can be bypassed by disabling scripts, editing the DOM or sending a direct request.

interviewBank.q: readonly or disabled — which one?
interviewBank.answer: readonly keeps the value visible and submitted but not editable. disabled removes it from submission, from the tab order and usually from the accessibility tree.

interviewBank.q: How do you add a pattern without making errors unusable?
interviewBank.answer: Keep the pattern simple and documented next to the field, give a concrete example, keep the label visible, and never rely on the pattern alone: validate again on the server and return a specific message.

defenseBank.q: A learner’s pattern does not match and they cannot see why.
defenseBank.answer: I test the pattern against a known-good value, check the anchors, and explain that pattern is fully anchored in HTML.

defenseBank.q: Why group radios in a fieldset?
defenseBank.answer: Without a legend the group has no question attached, so a screen-reader user hears the options but not what they are choosing.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute limits the number of characters a user can type?
mcqBank.why: maxlength caps the input length.

mcqBank.q: Which enctype is required for file uploads?
mcqBank.why: Files need the multipart encoding.

interviewBank.q: Why does autoplay often fail?
interviewBank.answer: Browsers block audible autoplay to protect users from unexpected sound. Muted autoplay is allowed, and playsinline keeps iOS from opening fullscreen.

interviewBank.q: What does the track element add?
interviewBank.answer: Timed text tracks: captions, subtitles, descriptions or chapters, linked to the media and selectable by the user.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between captions and subtitles?
interviewBank.answer: Captions transcribe dialogue and meaningful sounds for viewers who cannot hear the audio. Subtitles translate dialogue for viewers who can hear it but do not understand the language.

interviewBank.q: mp4 or webm — how do you choose?
interviewBank.answer: Offer both with source elements: mp4 with H.264 has the widest device support, webm often compresses better. The browser picks the first type it can play.

interviewBank.q: Why do browsers restrict autoplay?
interviewBank.answer: Unexpected sound is hostile to users and costly on mobile data, so browsers require a user gesture for audible playback. Muted autoplay and playsinline are the supported exceptions.

defenseBank.q: A learner’s video is black on iPhone.
defenseBank.answer: I check the codec and the playsinline attribute; Safari requires a supported codec and otherwise goes fullscreen.

defenseBank.q: Why are captions not optional?
defenseBank.answer: They are the text alternative for audio, and they also help in silent or noisy environments. Without them the media is inaccessible.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute shows the browser’s media controls?
mcqBank.why: controls renders play, pause and volume UI.

mcqBank.q: Which element links a caption file to a video?
mcqBank.why: track references the WebVTT file and its kind.

interviewBank.q: What is the first rule of ARIA?
interviewBank.answer: Do not use ARIA if a native element already provides the semantics. Native elements carry keyboard behaviour and accessibility support that a role alone does not.

interviewBank.q: What makes a focus indicator accessible?
interviewBank.answer: It must be visible against the background and not removed without an equivalent replacement. Keyboard users rely on it to know where they are.

interviewBank.q: What is the accessibility tree?
interviewBank.answer: The browser’s representation of the page for assistive technology: roles, names, states and relationships derived from the DOM, CSS and ARIA. It is what a screen reader actually navigates.

interviewBank.q: When is ARIA necessary?
interviewBank.answer: When no native element expresses the pattern, or when a native element needs an additional name, state or relationship. If a native element already provides the semantics, ARIA only adds risk.

interviewBank.q: How do you test keyboard accessibility?
interviewBank.answer: Unplug the mouse: tab through every control in a logical order, confirm a visible focus indicator, operate menus and dialogs with Enter, Space, Escape and arrows, and check that focus never disappears behind a layer.

defenseBank.q: A designer wants outline removed.
defenseBank.answer: I keep a visible custom focus style instead of removing it, because keyboard users lose their position otherwise.

defenseBank.q: How do you test accessibility without a screen reader?
defenseBank.answer: Keyboard-only navigation, the accessibility tree in dev tools and automated checks catch many issues, though a real screen-reader pass is still the reference.

mcqBank.q: Which element is keyboard accessible by default?
mcqBank.why: button is focusable and activates with Enter and Space.

mcqBank.q: What should a decorative image use?
mcqBank.why: An empty alt removes it from the accessibility tree.

interviewBank.q: Why is an iframe a performance and security concern?
interviewBank.answer: It loads a second document with its own resources and scripts. Without a sandbox it can navigate the top page, and it adds a network request that can delay the page.

interviewBank.q: When should content be embedded instead of linked?
interviewBank.answer: When the surrounding page needs it in context, such as a map or a video. If it is a full independent page, a link is simpler and safer.

interviewBank.q: What risks does an iframe introduce?
interviewBank.answer: It loads a second document with its own scripts and network access, can attempt top navigation and popups, adds a request that can delay the page, and can capture keyboard focus inside content you do not control.

interviewBank.q: What does a sandbox without allow-same-origin guarantee?
interviewBank.answer: The framed document gets an opaque origin: it cannot read cookies or storage for its own origin and cannot reach the parent through same-origin access. Combined with allow-scripts it can still run its own code.

interviewBank.q: When is an iframe the wrong tool?
interviewBank.answer: For embedding your own page structure, for navigation, and for layout. If the content is yours, render it in the document; if it is a full independent page, a link is safer and faster.

defenseBank.q: A learner embeds an untrusted widget with scripts and forms.
defenseBank.answer: I add sandbox and allow only what the widget needs, then verify the widget still works.
steps: Grant one permission at a time.

defenseBank.q: Why add a title to every iframe?
defenseBank.answer: The title is the only thing a screen-reader user hears before entering the frame, so it must name the embedded content.

mcqBank.why: The title attribute supplies the frame’s accessible name.

interviewBank.answer: It holds inert markup that is not rendered or executed. Scripts clone its content when the element is actually needed.

interviewBank.q: dialog or a custom modal div?
interviewBank.answer: dialog gives focus management, Escape handling, a backdrop and top-layer rendering natively. A div modal has to reimplement all of it and usually gets focus trapping wrong.

interviewBank.q: progress or meter?
interviewBank.answer: progress reports completion of a task and may be indeterminate. meter displays a measurement in a known range with low, high and optimum semantics.

interviewBank.q: What is the template element for?

interviewBank.q: Why keep CSS and JavaScript out of HTML?
interviewBank.answer: Each file has one responsibility, which makes caching, testing and reuse possible. Inline code also bypasses the content security policy and is harder to review.

interviewBank.q: What is the DOM and how does JavaScript change it?
interviewBank.answer: The DOM is the browser’s object model of the document. Scripts create, remove, move and modify nodes, and the browser re-renders the affected parts.

interviewBank.q: Where should script tags go, and why?
interviewBank.answer: In the head with defer for most pages: download starts early, execution waits for parsing and keeps document order. A classic script without defer blocks parsing and should sit at the end of body if it must.

interviewBank.q: How do HTML and JavaScript communicate without tight coupling?
interviewBank.answer: Through a small contract: ids for labels and fragments, data attributes for behaviour values, and events instead of inline handlers. The markup does not need to know how the script works.

interviewBank.q: What happens if the stylesheet fails to load?
interviewBank.answer: The HTML still renders in document order with the browser’s default styles. That is why structure and reading order must make sense without CSS, and why critical layout should not depend on a single remote file.

defenseBank.q: A learner styles everything inline for speed.
defenseBank.answer: Inline styles cannot be cached or reused and they override external rules, which makes later changes harder.

defenseBank.q: Why use data attributes instead of ids for behaviour?
defenseBank.answer: Ids must be unique and often carry styling or fragment meaning. A data attribute names the behaviour explicitly and can repeat.
steps: Keep ids for labels and fragments.

mcqBank.why: defer runs after parsing in document order.

interviewBank.q: How do you keep shared markup consistent without a framework?
